newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt calls Israel, PLO to end tunnel clashes.
newsitem.headline: Egypt calls Israel, PLO to end tunnel clashes.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak on Friday called on Israel and the Palestinians to halt three days of bloody clashes sparked by a controversial Israeli-dug tunnel, presidential sources said.
They said Mubarak telephoned both Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat several times and urged an end to the violence.
The sources did not give more details but Cairo newspapers said Mubarak had asked Israel to close the tunnel to end the bloodshed.

Fifty-three Palestinians and 13 Israelis have so far been killed in the violence which swept Jerusalem and the self-rule areas after Israel opened an archeological tunnel at the Temple Mount beside Islam's third holiest site, the al-Aqsa mosque.

"Mubarak has asked the Israeli government to shut the tunnel under the al-Aqsa as well as to implement with concrete steps the peace accords signed (with the Palestinians). This will be enough to calm the deteriorating situation," Friday's newspapers quoted goverment spokesman Safwat el-Sherif as saying.
Egypt has repeatedly called on Netanyahu to implement the accords which include trading occupied Arab lands for peace and redeploying troops from towns in the Palestinian West Bank.
Mubarak is also trying to arrange a meeting between Arafat and Netanyahu within the next few days.
The hardline Israeli premier told a news conference in Jerusalem that he would consider meeting Arafat in Cairo but added he would only talk peace after the violence had stopped.
In New York, Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa told the government-owned Al-Ahram newspaper that Egypt denounced the use of violence against the Palestinians.

"This use of violence against Palestinian civilians questions Israel's intentions towards the Palestinian Authority and the results of the peace process. These actions forecast a dangerous Israeli attitude," the daily quoted him as saying.
